answer: FCF is a management indicator derived from operating cash flow (OCF); it indicates how much cash is available for paying dividends or repaying debt at period end. Calculated: FCF excl. M&A (OCF after net PP&E/intangibles capex cash flow, cash outflow for leases and net interest paid) plus/minus cash flow from acquisitions/divestitures = FCF. So FCF excl. M&A = FCF before acquisitions and divestitures (2025: FCF 2,295 vs FCF excl. M&A 3,201 EUR m; difference = -906 M&A outflow). From 2026, FCF is replaced as the management indicator by FCF excl. M&A (to assess underlying operational performance and avoid wrong incentives given inorganic growth under Strategy 2030).

evidence.text: Free cash flow (FCF) is a management indicator derived from OCF. It is used as an indicator of how much cash is available to the company for paying out dividends or repaying debt
Starting from 2026, free cash flow will be replaced as a management indicator by free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures
FCF = Free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures ± Cash inflow/outflow from acquisitions/divestitures
